title: Checklist items not synced with fetched data
summary: When fetchChecklist completes, it updates state.currentChecklist in Redux, but the component uses local state checklistItems which is never populated from the Redux store.
failure_scenario: User clicks 'View Checklist' -> fetchChecklist thunk dispatches and Redux state updates -> component renders but checklistItems is still [] -> checklist appears empty even though Redux has data
impact: Users see no checklist items to complete, breaking the entire tracker feature

title: fetchChecklist dispatch not awaited properly for Redux state update
summary: fetchChecklist is dispatched but the component doesn't wait for the Redux state to update before trying to use checklist data. Also, the function doesn't check if fetchChecklist actually succeeded.
code_context:
await dispatch(fetchChecklist(appId)) (line 73)
Immediately after, setActiveTab('checklist') (line 72)
No check for resultAction.fulfilled.match() like in handleCreateApplication
failure_scenario: User clicks 'View Checklist', dispatch happens, but if there's a network error or invalid app_id, no error is shown and checklist tab appears empty
impact: Silent failures - user doesn't know if the API call failed or the data is just empty

title: saveChecklist error state not shown to user
summary: saveChecklist thunk rejection updates Redux error state, but LegalIdDetail never displays errors from saveChecklist. The error banner on line 55 only shows when error && !currentGuidance, not during save operations.
code_context:
handleSaveChecklist calls dispatch(saveChecklist(...)) (line 87-94)
No check for resultAction.fulfilled or .rejected
Error state exists in Redux but UI never displays it
failure_scenario: User saves checklist, API returns 403 Forbidden due to ownership check, Redux error updates, but UI shows 'Save Checklist' button as if nothing happened - user has no idea the save failed
impact: Data loss perception - user thinks changes are saved when they're not

title: selectedService used in API call without validation
summary: handleCreateApplication only checks if selectedService is falsy, but doesn't validate that the service actually exists in guidance.services array.
failure_scenario: If frontend form validation is removed or bypassed (via devtools), user can submit arbitrary service names, causing backend 400 error with no frontend error handling shown to user
impact: Backend returns 400 detail 'Service not found', but UI has no error display for createApplication failures

title: createApplication thunk success doesn't clear trackerLoading reliably
summary: If createApplication is rejected (line 64), trackerLoading is only cleared in the finally block. However, no success toast/alert is shown, and the modal closes without confirming to user that creation succeeded.
failure_scenario: User creates application, modal closes, user doesn't know if it actually succeeded or if modal just closed due to error. Later they see duplicate application entry.

title: Unsafe status color mapping with type assertion
summary: statusColors is defined but the mapping could fail silently if app.status has an unexpected value. The as keyof typeof statusColors assertion masks type errors.
failure_scenario: Backend returns app.status = 'unknown' (due to data corruption or API bug), statusBgColor becomes undefined, no CSS class applied, status badge has no styling
impact: Visual bug - status badge renders without styling, confusing users

title: No error display for fetchApplications failure
summary: fetchApplications can reject and update state.error, but LegalIdHub only renders error if isLoading && error appears above idTypes grid (line 54). The My Applications section (line 93) never shows error state - it will just appear empty.
code_context:
Error display (lines 54-57) only affects idTypes grid
My Applications section (lines 93-159) has no error handling
If fetchApplications fails, applications = [] and user sees 'You haven't tracked any applications yet' with no error message
failure_scenario: Network error when fetching applications, Redux error updates, but user sees empty state with CTA to start tracking instead of error message
impact: User confusion - they think there are no applications when API failed

title: Checklist items use non-unique keys if item.id is missing
summary: Checklist items are rendered with key={item.id} but if item.id is undefined or null, React will render all items with key=undefined, causing re-render bugs.
failure_scenario: Backend returns ChecklistItem without id field (schema validation bypassed), all checkboxes share same key=undefined, toggling one checkbox toggles all; React warns about duplicate keys
impact: Critical rendering bug - checkboxes malfunction, user can't track which items are done

title: Services rendered with array index key (anti-pattern)
summary: Services grid uses key={idx} instead of unique identifier. While services are static, this is poor practice and breaks React key semantics.
failure_scenario: If guidance data is mutated (service list reordered), React may reuse DOM nodes incorrectly, causing state to leak between cards
impact: Potential visual bugs if services list is reordered; violates React best practices

title: FAQs rendered with array index key (anti-pattern)
summary: FAQs grid uses key={idx} instead of using FAQ content hash or unique identifier.
failure_scenario: If FAQs are reordered, React may reuse DOM nodes, causing open/closed state to apply to wrong FAQ
impact: Details state (open/closed) may leak between FAQs if list is reordered

title: Documents required rendered with array index key
summary: Document list uses key={idx} - fine for static data but violates React patterns.
failure_scenario: Low risk since documents_required is static, but if dynamic in future, reordering breaks React semantics
impact: Minor - unlikely to cause issues with static data

title: Unsafe error object cast in fetchIdTypes
summary: Error handling casts err as { response?: { data?: { detail?: string } } } but if error structure differs (e.g., timeout, network error), response is undefined and error message defaults to generic string.
code_context:
const error = err as { response?: { data?: { detail?: string } } }
return rejectWithValue(error.response?.data?.detail || 'Failed to load ID types')
failure_scenario: Network timeout occurs, error.response is undefined, generic error shown. User sees 'Failed to load ID types' with no context (timeout vs 500 error)
impact: Poor error messaging - users can't distinguish between network issues and server errors

title: No validation that API response matches IdApplication type
summary: createApplication thunk doesn't validate that response.data is actually an IdApplication. If backend returns invalid data, no error is thrown.
failure_scenario: Backend returns { id: null, id_type: undefined, status: 'invalid' } (due to backend bug), app silently stores invalid data in Redux, later operations crash
impact: Silent data corruption - invalid data stored in Redux without warning

title: Local checklistItems never initialized from Redux currentChecklist
summary: Even though fetchChecklist updates Redux state.currentChecklist, the component local state checklistItems is never populated. User sees empty checklist.
code_context:
const [checklistItems, setChecklistItems] = useState<ChecklistItem[]>([]) (line 30)
No useEffect to sync: setChecklistItems(currentChecklist) when fetchChecklist completes
failure_scenario: User views checklist, Redux updates with 5 items, but component renders 0 checklistItems, so no checkboxes appear. User must refresh page to see items (if they know to do that).
impact: Critical UX - entire checklist feature broken

title: userAppsForThisId computed before idType or applications updated
summary: userAppsForThisId is computed on every render, but if idType changes or applications fetch completes with delay, it may be stale or filter empty.
code_context:
const userAppsForThisId = applications.filter((app) => app.id_type === idType) (line 46)
If dispatch(fetchApplications()) completes asynchronously, first renders may show empty array
failure_scenario: User navigates to /legal-id/aadhaar, component mounts, fetchApplications dispatched, but filter runs before async thunk completes, so userAppsForThisId is empty for 1-2 seconds
impact: Minor visual jank - applications flicker in/out

title: app.id passed to handleViewChecklist but function parameter expects appId: string
summary: app.id is typed as string in IdApplication, but if API returns app.id = null or undefined, no runtime error occurs until fetch attempts.
code_context:
onClick={() => handleViewChecklist(app.id, app.service)} (line 209)
handleViewChecklist function doesn't validate appId before dispatch(fetchChecklist(appId))
failure_scenario: Backend returns { id: null }, user clicks 'View Checklist', fetchChecklist(null) dispatches to /applications/null/checklist which returns 404, error updates Redux but UI doesn't display it
impact: Silent API call to wrong endpoint, user sees no feedback

title: Status formatting logic duplicated in 3 places
summary: app.status formatting appears at lines 129-132, 139-140, 205-206, 477-478. Should be extracted to utility function.
code_context:
app.status.replace('_', ' ').split(' ').map(...).join(' ') repeated 4 times
StatusColor mapping also duplicated (lines 111-116, 188-193, 461-466)
failure_scenario: If status enum changes, all 4 locations must be updated. Missing one causes inconsistency.

title: idType from useParams not validated before API calls
summary: idType is extracted from URL params but never validated. User can navigate to /legal-id/invalid-type and component calls fetchIdGuidance('invalid-type').
failure_scenario: User manually types /legal-id/xyz in URL, component fetches guidance for 'xyz', backend returns 404, error shown is 'ID type 'xyz' not found' - this works but backend is doing validation that frontend should do
impact: Minor - backend validation catches it, but frontend could fail faster

title: ID type cards use key={idType.key} which is string, not unique ID
summary: While idType.key should be unique, it's not guaranteed to be a valid React key if it contains special chars or is user-controlled.
failure_scenario: If idType.key = 'aadhaar/pan' (contains /), React may warn. Very edge-casey.
impact: Minimal - unlikely idType.key would be invalid
